significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that reversal failures arise because "subject-position enrichment binds attributes in one direction only," with the resulting decodability asymmetry predicting reverse-recall accuracy and varying with textual bidirectionality; this is primarily a form-(iii) predictive coupling plus a form-(ii) mechanism, not merely an existence claim. It would establish both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanism, resolving the consequential storage-versus-directional-access distinction left open by the behavioral Reversal Curse result of Berglund et al. (2023), while constraining expectations for other relation types and reverse-training interventions. Verified-false and verified-true are distinguishable: failure of the predicted locus, coupling, or bidirectionality dependence would rule out this specific subject-anchored account, although it would not by itself identify the alternative mechanism. The topic-substitution check lowers the case from a top score: generic query-dependent retrieval is an obvious topic-level hypothesis, but the specific subject locus and cross-relation quantitative coupling are claim-specific and justify an above-median score.

reach.justification: The named handle is the "decodability asymmetry as a quantitative index of the curse," together with the implied intervention of explicitly writing reverse associations during training. The index is principally a diagnostic but can be ex ante when used to predict reverse-recall failures or "which relations and training interventions can mitigate" them before deployment decisions, providing an action window rather than only explaining observed errors. After per-model probe re-extraction, the substantive prediction—greater directional decodability asymmetry implies worse reverse recall, with lower asymmetry for textually bidirectional relations—still specifies what should be found; its asserted scope spans relation classes and language models, with likely uptake by interpretability researchers and model trainers or auditors. The topic-substitution check passes: the topic alone supplies no transferable index or mitigation rule, whereas these specific handles support reach above the median, though the claim does not establish broad non-AI uptake or a calibration-free deployment screen.
